artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation summary: scope excursion promoted into an 18-class seed enum across 10 files, grouping-time case/separator folding plus an empty alias-table mechanism added to the conclusion aggregator, repeated --tasks (and a repeated mode flag) rejected with a usage error, class gained a shape convention and append-time warnings, 10 new regression cases each proven non-vacuous, and the deploy re-verified clean.

completion_data.completion_summary: Promoted scope excursion into an 18-class issue-log seed enum (10 files reconciled), added grouping-time case/separator folding with an empty alias-table mechanism and class_variants/variants auditability to orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh, rejected a repeated --tasks (and mode) flag with a usage error, added a class shape convention plus append-time warnings to issue-record.sh, and added 10 new regression cases -- all verified against the deployed tree after redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan requires proving a new regression case is non-vacuous (fails when the fix is reverted), the cheapest technique for a git-tracked source-store script is: `git show <pre-fix-commit>:path/to/script.sh > scratch/copy.sh` into a disposable scratch harness (never touching the live tree), then re-run the new test's exact assertion logic directly against that old copy. For a direction no historical commit exhibits (e.g. proving a byte-identity HARD CONSTRAINT case would catch a rewrite, or that an over-merge-rejection case would catch an over-eager alias-table entry), deliberately inject the bug into a scratch copy instead (sed/python patch) and confirm the assertion then fails. Both are fast (seconds) and require no test-file changes.

An apostrophe inside a comment or prose string written INSIDE a single-quoted bash heredoc-less jq script literal (e.g. `jq -s '... # issue-record.sh's own helper ...'`) silently closes the enclosing bash single-quote early, producing a confusing bash -n syntax error pointing at an unrelated later line. Caught immediately by `bash -n` before any test run. Avoid apostrophes in any comment text written inside a single-quoted jq/awk/sed script embedded in a bash script -- rephrase to avoid the possessive form entirely.

scripts/tests/test-common-lib.sh has a pre-existing, reproducible environment-leak defect: its 'mode=deploy-tree-first (both exist)' case fails whenever CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store is exported in the ambient environment before running it directly (3/3 reproductions), while it passes cleanly (3/3) with the variable unset. This surfaces as a false-looking NEW failure whenever a broad verify-touched.sh narrowed battery happens to select test-common-lib.sh under that override (e.g. for an unrelated task's source-store-mode phase verification). Not caused by editing lib/common.sh or test-common-lib.sh itself; confirmed by reproducing with zero other files touched.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh class grouping
sapience_notes.value: Grouping-time normalization (case + separator folding) must stay strictly separate from any semantic merge: the five 'scope' class spellings found in the evidence base are NOT five spellings of one concept -- scope/file_scope omission (scope found too narrow) is plausibly the opposite concept from scope excursion (work falling outside a declared scope) -- so the mechanical fold deliberately leaves differently-worded classes unmerged, and a curated alias table for semantic merges ships empty rather than pre-populated.

sapience_notes.subject: issue-log.md class field validation
sapience_notes.value: A verb/keyword blocklist (flagging class values containing 'confirmed', 'found', 'discovered') to catch free-text-sentence class values was rejected: the corpus shows this would false-positive against widespread legitimate kind:win usage (e.g. 'hypothesis confirmed', 'blocker-cleared', 'falsifiability confirmed'). The remedy that actually discriminates sentence-shaped values from legitimate short noun phrases is the existing outside-the-seed-enum stderr warning, extended to name a documented class-shape convention, plus an independent post-fold token-count (>6) style warning as a secondary signal.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh OWED fallback
sapience_notes.value: A prose-only doc file (e.g. a .md contract/standard with no dedicated test suite) touched alongside script files in one verify-touched.sh invocation triggers the OWED-NOT-PAID fallback for that unmapped path, which runs the entire free-cost-class suite battery rather than a narrow suite subset -- this can multiply a scoped verification's wall-clock cost substantially (observed: a 12-path call with 2 unmapped doc paths ran 31 suites / 98 assertions and took several minutes under the harness's default foreground timeout, auto-backgrounding the call).

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh deploy-root-guard.sh
sapience_notes.value: orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh and issue-record.sh both refuse to run directly from the agent-system source store under every flag, including --help -- deploy-root-guard.sh is sourced before argument parsing. A manual scratch smoke-test of either script's new warning/rejection logic must either deploy first or copy the script into a scratch .claude/scripts/ tree (as the test harnesses already do via common_test_resolve_subject with CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store); running the raw source-store copy directly always errors out before any of the new logic executes.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh index-entries.json regeneration
sapience_notes.value: deploy-headless.sh runs generate-context-line-counts.sh --write automatically as part of its own pipeline before verification, so a hand-edit that changes a context file's line count (e.g. adding two new sections to issue-log.md) never needs its index-entries.json line_count field corrected by hand -- only the summary/prose fields are the implementer's responsibility; line_count drift self-heals at the next deploy.

sapience_notes.subject: jq group_by representative selection
sapience_notes.value: A deterministic most-frequent-value-with-lexicographic-tie-break selection from a jq array is expressible in one reusable idiom: `$raws | group_by(.) | map({v: .[0], c: length}) | sort_by(.v) | sort_by(-.c) | .[0].v` -- jq's sort_by/sort are stable sorts, so sorting ascending by value first and then descending by count second leaves ties in alphabetical order, giving the lexicographically-smallest value among the most frequent ones without a separate tie-break branch.
